fields.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period.
fields.note: The document supports the cap formula, the negative-CPI rule, the June 30 publication with September 1 effect, owner petitions decided within 60 days, and the written notice duty. It does not mention the 2.87% rate for 2026-27, tenant petitions, or the registration-fee pass-through and $50 reimbursement. Those come from D084, which is not in this document.

fields.quoted_span: If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.
fields.note: The lower of 3% or 80% of CPI and the no-increase-if-negative rule are supported. The 2.87% rate for Sept 1, 2026 through Aug 31, 2027 and the $50 pass-through cap do not appear in this document.

fields.quoted_span: The new ordinances are not effective until November 19, 2021.
The new ordinances are not effective until November 19, 2021.
fields.note: The document shows the ordinance taking effect on Nov 19, 2021 and nothing about repeal. It does not explicitly state that the ordinance is currently in force.

fields.quoted_span: The rent cap does not apply to residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995, or to mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990.
fields.note: The document says only 'constructed', so the year_built basis is an inference. The rule's construction_date_basis field already flags this.

fields.quoted_span: a Rent Stabilization Ordinance, which limits residential rent increases to no more than 3% per year
fields.note: The document names the Rent Stabilization Ordinance and its 2021 effective date. It gives no municipal code section.
